text: `@Override` has no members and `SOURCE` retention, so it is discarded before the class file exists. Its entire effect is a rule enforced by the ___ .
explanation: It is not a modifier and it does not change dispatch — overriding happens whether you write it or not. It is an assertion: if the marked method overrides nothing, report an error. That is the third kind of annotation reader, after nobody and the running program, and `@SuppressWarnings` and `@FunctionalInterface` are the same. One line turns Chapter 20's silent `equals(Point)` bug into a compile error.
